name: Ouroboros Energy Thermal Glider — 'The Lammergeier'
description:
The Lammergeier is an unpowered thermal soaring platform developed by Ouroboros Energy as a byproduct of their atmospheric heat mapping research — the company needed a low-cost, long-endurance observation platform for monitoring thermal columns above their industrial energy installations, and the result was a vehicle that accidentally became one of the most capable covert aerial platforms in GLMZ. The airframe is a swept-wing glider with a 9-meter wingspan built from aerogel-composite panels that are nearly invisible on radar and produce no heat signature because the vehicle carries no engine. Lift is generated entirely through exploitation of thermal columns — the rising heat plumes produced in abundance by GLMZ's industrial density.

The Lammergeier's Thermal Navigation System is the vehicle's core intelligence — a suite of atmospheric pressure and temperature sensors linked to a predictive soaring algorithm that identifies and routes the glider between thermal columns with minimal operator input. An experienced pilot can fly indefinitely over the industrial districts, riding the city's waste heat as fuel. The vehicle seats one in a prone configuration, reducing frontal profile to under 0.4 square meters. Communication and sensor systems are passive-only by default — the glider listens and observes without transmitting, making it electronically silent during operations. Data is stored onboard and offloaded after landing.

The Lammergeier is used by Ouroboros for legitimate atmospheric monitoring, but the platform's properties — no engine, no emissions, no active transmissions, radar-near-invisible — make it extraordinarily attractive for surveillance, courier drops, and infiltration overwatch. It is not fast and it cannot operate in rain or low-thermal conditions, but over the right terrain and under the right atmospheric conditions, it is effectively undetectable. Operators who know GLMZ's thermal geography can cross the entire city without touching the ground.

specifications.endurance: Indefinite over active thermal terrain; 90 minutes over cold terrain

tactical_use: The Lammergeier is deployed for extended aerial surveillance, overwatch positioning, and courier drop operations where the use of a powered aircraft would trigger detection or licensing review. Intelligence operatives use it to observe target locations over multiple hours without generating any detectable signature. The cargo hardpoint accepts sensor pods, drop packages, or communication relay nodes. In infiltration operations, the glider serves as an insertion platform — a pilot can approach a target facility from altitude and land on rooftop access points with near-zero acoustic signature. Extraction by Lammergeier requires thermal conditions that allow takeoff, which limits its reliability as an exfil platform.
cultural_context: The Lammergeier is named for a bone-eating vulture, a choice that reflects both the vehicle's soaring profile and Ouroboros Energy's habit of naming products after scavengers and cycles. Among the small community of operators who use the platform, there is a pronounced culture of atmospheric expertise — Lammergeier pilots develop detailed personal knowledge of GLMZ's thermal geography, tracking how industrial output cycles affect soaring conditions at different times of day and season. This knowledge is considered proprietary and is rarely shared. The best Lammergeier pilots in the city are known by reputation only, identified by the cargo they've delivered and the things they've seen.
story_hooks: A Lammergeier was found landed on the roof of a secure facility with no pilot aboard — the cargo hardpoint was empty, but the onboard sensor log captured twelve hours of data that someone clearly wanted.

Ouroboros Energy's atmospheric monitoring program has been producing reports that don't match public data — someone is using the Lammergeier fleet to observe things that have nothing to do with thermal columns.

The players need aerial overwatch for an operation in a district with active anti-air defenses. The only platform that can operate there undetected is a Lammergeier, and the one pilot who knows those thermals wants something in return.
A Lammergeier pilot has been missing for three days. Their last known position was directly above a corporate black site, and the onboard data recorder is somewhere in the facility below.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, predatory swept-wing glider with an elongated fuselage tapering to a needle-sharp tail boom. The airframe resembles a raptor in flight — angular, minimalist, almost skeletal. The canopy is a teardrop of dark tinted composite barely visible against the airframe. No visible engine, no protruding hardware. Designed to disappear visually at distance.
physical_description.dimensions: 9.2m wingspan (folds to 1.8m for transport); fuselage length 7.1m; overall height when standing on landing gear 1.2m. Palm-sized from ground at operational altitude.
physical_description.weight_description: Approximately 85 kg dry weight. Handheld and portable when wings are folded — transportable by two operators or carried via reinforced drone carrier. Landing gear is retractable.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerogel-composite panel construction throughout airframe and control surfaces. Hollow-core composite spars. Thermally inert polymeric resin matrix.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with light-absorbing nanopolymer topcoat. Surfaces are deliberately non-reflective to minimize visual signature. Minimal surface texture — smooth except for barely-perceptible airflow management riblets.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal-gray primary with deep midnight blue accents along leading edges. Underside is flat black. Canopy frame is gunmetal. No reflective markings visible from distance.
physical_description.interface_elements: Single pilot bubble canopy with manual transparency controls and emergency eject mechanism. Minimal cockpit — analog airspeed indicator, altitude variometer, artificial horizon, thermal column detection display (soft-glow amber readout visible only from pilot position). Single sidestick control column. Hard-wired mechanical pitch/roll inputs — no fly-by-wire. Passive thermal and pressure sensor array scattered across upper wing surfaces (barely visible black dots). Data storage module mounted in ventral fuselage. Cargo hardpoint beneath fuselage with manual release mechanism.
distinctive_features: Swept-wing planform at near-extreme angle — appears perpetually in a knife-edge climb stance
Visible thermal sensor nodules along upper wing surfaces — small black hemispheres in geometric pattern
Retractable landing gear with spring-loaded forks — minimizes ground profile
Feathered trim tabs and winglets that adjust autonomously in response to thermal conditions
Canopy reflection suppression mesh barely visible as fine pattern overlay
Three-axis control surfaces with mechanical advantage design — no redundancy, pure efficiency
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Ouroboros Energy logo (stylized serpent eating its tail, 3cm) on upper right wing root in flat gray. Small 'LAMMERGEIER' designation in 2cm sans-serif on tail boom. Manufacturer compliance codes printed on interior fuselage bulkhead (not visible without canopy removal). Registration QR code on lower fuselage in monochrome only.
physical_description.condition_typical: Flight-worn finish with dust accumulation on upper surfaces from airflow exposure. Occasional thermal stress discoloration (faint tan marks) where aerogel panels experience repeated heating cycles. Canopy may show light haze from atmospheric particulate. Landing gear and fittings show scuffing from repeated field launches. No visible maintenance access panels — aircraft is intended for minimal serviceable units.

image_prompt: Product photography of a matte charcoal swept-wing glider aircraft with 9-meter span, needle-sharp fuselage, and dark tinted canopy, positioned at three-quarter angle on a concrete landing pad at GLMZ industrial district with smoking thermal vents and factory skyline in background. Dramatic raking sidelight reveals aerogel-composite panel structure and subtle thermal sensor array on upper wing. Minimal ground shadow emphasizes weightless design. Adjacent detail shot shows pilot prone position through semi-transparent canopy overlay and mechanical sidestick control interface.
